transcript: World War 3 won't start with a bomb. It will start with your food. Yes, you heard it right. Over the last 3 weeks, something strange started happening across Europe. Fridges and freezers inside supermarkets suddenly began heating up on their own. Ice cream melted, meat went bad, and trolleys of food got dumped. And this was not a power cut. It was a hacker. Because today, even supermarket fridges run on the internet. And someone slipped in and turned the temperature up to 50°. An oven overnight. It started in France, where 700 stores lost everything in one night. Then it spread. Sweden, Belgium, Ireland, the Netherlands, Finland, one after another. And it was not only Europe. Around the same time, similar failures hit stores and military bases in America. But here it gets strange. Nobody asked for money. Nobody took the credit. And they did not go after banks or secrets. They went after food, the most basic thing we all need. All while Europe keeps seeing strange attacks on its basic systems. Even the experts cannot agree. Some call it bored young hackers. Others call attacking a country's food an act of war. But here is the real question: if someone can quietly switch off a whole country's food from a laptop, what do you think they'd go after next? The water, the power, the hospitals? It could be literally anything. Going after a country's food hurts normal people more than any government. So is attacking the food supply ever fair game? Or is this a line nobody should cross? Drop your take in the comments and follow for more such breakthroughs.
caption:
Hackers Are Now Targeting Your Food

For years hackers chased money. Now they are going after the food sitting on supermarket shelves instead.
Across Europe, fridges in stores were switched to defrost and everything inside was spoiled by morning.
